user.title: Batocera
user.description: Connect a Batocera box. The MQTT integration must be set up first.

install.title: Install on the box
install.description:
Home Assistant connects to the box over SSH as root, adds an SSH key of its own to root's authorized keys, and installs the ha-batocera daemon. From then on it uses that key to keep the daemon up to date.

The box needs an account of its own on your MQTT broker: create one, and enter it under Advanced with the broker's address as the box reaches it. If the broker uses ACLs, give the account [these rights]({acls}). With Advanced left empty, Home Assistant looks for the broker from the box, and uses it if it needs no account.

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the box.
data_description.password: Batocera's default root password is linux. It is used for this install only and is not stored.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: The broker as the box reaches it, and the box's account on it. If any of these is filled in, Home Assistant looks for nothing and uses them as given.

data_description.mqtt_host: An address on your network, not core-mosquitto or localhost.
data_description.mqtt_user: Empty if the broker needs no account.

install_mosquitto.title: Install on the box
install_mosquitto.description:
Home Assistant connects to the box over SSH as root, adds an SSH key of its own to root's authorized keys, and installs the ha-batocera daemon. From then on it uses that key to keep the daemon up to date.

Home Assistant will add an MQTT user for this box to the Mosquitto add-on and restart it. Devices on MQTT reconnect within seconds.

data_description.name: The box's MQTT topics go under batocera/ and this name, in lower case, with underscores for spaces.
data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the box.
data_description.password: Batocera's default root password is linux. It is used for this install only and is not stored.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Another broker, as the box reaches it, and the box's account on it. If any of these is filled in, Home Assistant adds no user to the add-on and uses them as given.

data_description.mqtt_host: An address on your network, not core-mosquitto or localhost.
data_description.mqtt_user: Empty if the broker needs no account.

manual.title: Box already set up
manual.description: Connect a box where the ha-batocera daemon was installed by hand.

data_description.topic: batocera/ and the device name set in ha-batocera.conf on the box.

reconfigure.title: Pair again
reconfigure.description: Home Assistant connects with the root password, trusts the SSH host key the box has now, replaces its own SSH key on the box and reinstalls the daemon. The settings on the box are kept.

data_description.password: Used for this step only, not stored.

host_key_mismatch.title: {name}: SSH host key changed
host_key_mismatch.description:
The SSH host key of {name} ({host}) is not the one Home Assistant trusted when it was set up, so Home Assistant does not connect to it and does not update the ha-batocera daemon.

If Batocera was reinstalled or the key was replaced on purpose, reconfigure the Batocera integration for this box with the root password: it then trusts the new key. If not, something on your network may be posing as the box.

update_failed.title: {name}: cannot update ha-batocera
update_failed.description:
Home Assistant could not check or update the ha-batocera daemon on {name} ({host}): {error}

It tries again the next time the box comes online, or when the integration is reloaded. If the box no longer accepts Home Assistant's SSH key, reconfigure the Batocera integration for this box with the root password.

public_web_access.title: {name}: EmulationStation's web API is open to the network
public_web_access.description:
EmulationStation on {name} accepts commands on port 1234 from the whole network, without authentication: its PublicWebAccess setting is on. Anyone on your network can launch or quit games and send input to them. The limits set here still stop a game launched while the box is locked, but only once it has started. ha-batocera itself uses this API from the box only, and never changes this setting.

To restrict the API to the box, log in to the box as root and run these commands, which stop EmulationStation while the setting changes (it rewrites its settings when it exits), then start it again:

```
/etc/init.d/S31emulationstation stop
sed -i 's/"PublicWebAccess" value="true"/"PublicWebAccess" value="false"/' /userdata/system/configs/emulationstation/es_settings.cfg
/etc/init.d/S31emulationstation start
```

This warning goes away by itself once the box reports the setting off: it checks when the daemon starts and every 30 minutes while no game runs.

init.title: Who may play
init.description: Everyone who can open Home Assistant sees what is playing and browses the games. Launching, pausing and stopping games, and shutting the box down and powering it on, is for admins, and for the users picked here. Automations may always do it.

data.control_users: Users who may launch, pause and stop games, and power the box on and off

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Where Power on sends its Wake-on-LAN packet. Empty, the box's own: it reports them while it is on, and Home Assistant keeps the last ones for when it is off.

data_description.wake_mac: Of the box's network card, as aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.
data_description.wake_broadcast: Of the box's subnet, as 192.168.1.255. Empty, and not reported by the box, the packet goes to 255.255.255.255, which may leave from another network than the box's.
